newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George says on track for forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George says on track for forecasts.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Thursday it was on track to meet earnings forecasts made when it announced its merger with Advance Bank.
"Yes, we're on track," said managing director Jim Sweeney told reporters, when asked if St George was on track to meet its earnings forecasts.
"We are working very hard to meet our earnings predictions as we put out in the memorandum document to our shareholders," Sweeney said.
St George said when announcing its A$2.65 billion friendly takeover of Advance Bank Ltd in October that the merger would increase earnings per share before the deduction of goodwill.

St George said earlier this month that trading in the first quarter of the year to June 30, 1997 had been satisfactory. It has previously said it expected a flatter result in 1996/97 than the 9.4 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$148.3 million.
Sweeney also said St George's credit rating upgrade from Standard and Poors and Moody's would help improve the group's performance because it would open up new funding avenues.
"It opens up availability of credit where previously, particularly European and large U.S. banks and investment houses will only invest in certain parts of the credit curve," he said.
"The higher the rating you have, the better the type of deal you can negotiate on price," he said. Sweeney said he could not give an absolute figure for the benefit.
"As a general statement, we'll be able to raise our offshore funding more cheaply than we were able to before," he said.

Standard and Poors said last month it had raised its long-term and short-term counterparty ratings for St George Bank to A/A1 from A minus/A2 because of the bank's improved medium term profitability outlook because of the marger.
St George shares closed down one cent at A$7.77 on Thursday.
